value.title: In-process UTC offset and process ancestry (issues #127, #128)
value.summary: Two daemon launch sites go to zero at steady state: the per-pending-Claude-seat `/bin/date` for the UTC offset (#127, a per-tick-per-seat launch AGENTS.md forbids) and the per-ancestor `/bin/ps` in registration (#128). Both become in-process reads, each with a before and after counter reading and a spawn_sites guard.

sections.name: summary
sections.value: Found by the performance seat (governance roles/performance/memory/2026-11-06-spawn-attribution.md, file:line at f327a7d). Pre-existing since 03ab38e; not caused by s04. Doesn't gate the PEC try-out, so it sits behind the s05 critical path. Delivery (pij-swift-kestrel) owns claude_bind: if another coder takes this, kestrel reviews the bind change.

sections.name: goals
value: Two daemon launch sites go to zero at steady state: the per-pending-Claude-seat `/bin/date` for the UTC offset (#127, a per-tick-per-seat launch AGENTS.md forbids) and the per-ancestor `/bin/ps` in registration (#128). Both become in-process reads, each with a before and after counter reading and a spawn_sites guard.

sections.name: non_goals
value: Anything another roadmap step owns; see roadmap 001.

value.claim: #127, UTC offset in-process. `crates/harnesses/src/proc.rs:322-327` computes the local UTC offset in-process (the time crate's local offset or libc localtime_r's tm_gmtoff) instead of launching `date`; every caller (claude_bind's loop at claude_bind.rs:73,90 from lib.rs:669-673, FYI claim and read, carrier flush, Claude adopt, revive, double-seat) gets the same value as before.

#128, ancestry in-process (ruling C27). `crates/daemon/src/registration.rs` reads each ancestor's parent and kernel name in-process (macOS proc_pidinfo short BSD info; Linux /proc as before) and launches `/bin/ps` for argv only when the name is a harness host's (copilot, claude, codex, node), so a registration launches at most 1 ps instead of one per ancestor. The 32-ancestor cap and the results for native and paneless registration are unchanged. `unsafe_code = "forbid"` stays absolute (C27).

Guards. crates/testkit/tests/spawn_sites.rs fails if a `date` launch returns on the UTC-offset path, or if registration's `ps` is reached other than through the host-name gate; a registration test counts at most 1 argv read per registration (C27).

Readings. The performance seat records, on the live fleet before and after deploy, `date.utc-offset` and `ps.registration-native-process` over a 60 s at-rest window with pending Claude seats present (expected: date.utc-offset to 0; ps.registration-native-process at most 1 per registration, C27), plus the daemon total, with data.pid on each reading.

Cost (AGENTS.md, resource cost is a correctness property). Removes launches: date.utc-offset to 0, and ps.registration-native-process from one per ancestor to at most 1 per registration (C27); no new launch, loop or timer. The before and after readings are AC4.

Docs and states. No roadmap or PRD state changes (an issue fix). The PR closes #127 and #128; docs/difficulties.md gets a resolved row. docs/how/pij-rs-api.md documents new verbs and refusals; the skill's verb coverage tables carry them; `just ddocs-check` and `ddocs validate` on the project docs pass; the PR body has a `Delivers:` line.

sections.value: Code: crates/harnesses/src/proc.rs:322-327; crates/daemon/src/claude_bind.rs:73,90; crates/daemon/src/lib.rs:669-673; crates/core/src/config.rs:201; crates/daemon/src/registration.rs:223, :437, :1647-1662; crates/testkit/tests/spawn_sites.rs. If a new dependency is needed (the time crate's local-offset feature or libproc), keep it to the smallest one and say why; the lockfile allowlist applies.

value.question: #128: argv on macOS needs sysctl(KERN_PROCARGS2), which needs unsafe; the workspace forbids it and no safe crate works (sysctl 0.7.1 ENOENT; sysinfo lists every pid). Allow one audited unsafe function (A) or read argv with ps only for host-named ancestors (B)?
value.answer: Ruling C27 (prime, 2026-11-06): B. unsafe_code = "forbid" stays absolute; A is reopened only if measurements show registration still hurts.

value.risk: Two lanes edit the same CLI wiring or skill files.
value.mitigation: Rebase onto main before the PR; small diffs at the seam; pm-001 orders merges.

sections.name: execution_guardrails
value: Tests use scratch repos and a private daemon; never the live governance branch or the prod daemon.
Builds: your own target or `just shared-build`; CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0; -p scoping; stop under 25 GB free.
No `git add -A`, no `--no-verify`; no node_modules, never symlinked (C25); TS proof is CI on the exact head.
Shared seams (crates/cli wiring, skills/pij): rebase onto main before the PR and keep edits minimal; don't fork the seam.
One push per review round; no pushes after the PR is out for verdicts unless a verdict asks.
